topic: Mlai senior scenario ambiguous problem framing
question: As the senior ML lead, how would you turn this into an actionable, well-scoped ML problem?
idealAnswer:
Push to define engagement concretely and measurably before any modeling starts, e.g. session length, return visit rate, content interactions, since different definitions imply different models and different tradeoffs

Identify what decision or action the model output would actually drive, e.g. re-ranking content, triggering a notification, personalizing a homepage, an ML problem needs a clear point of intervention, not just an abstract goal

Push back on vague goals by proposing a specific, measurable success metric and a way to validate impact, e.g. an A/B test plan, before committing engineering time to build anything

Consider unintended consequences of naively optimizing engagement, e.g. optimizing for pure time-on-platform can incentivize addictive or low-quality content, a senior answer flags this risk proactively

Mentions aligning stakeholders, product and other teams with competing definitions, on a shared definition and success criteria early, since misalignment discovered after building the model is far more costly
